result.title: ECOS: Environment-Calibrated On-Policy Self-Distillation for Language Agents
result.summary: On-policy self-distillation lets a language agent act as its own Teacher by conditioning on privileged context such as skills written from its own trajectories. Its guidance, however, is weighted by how much this context shifts token likelihoods rather than by whether it improves behavior, so errors in self-written skills return through later updates. We propose environment-calibrated on-policy self-distillation, which uses environmental outcomes to decide how much to trust the Teacher's current guidance and which self-written skills to reinforce. Command-level advantages, estimated by comparing commands executed at similar observations, scale each Teacher preference and reward reflections and skills whose induced preferences favor higher-advantage commands. Without skills at inference, 3B and 7B agents reach 90.5% and 93.3% macro success on seen ALFWorld tasks and 75.5% and 80.5% success on WebShop. On unseen ALFWorld tasks, they outperform GRPO under the same protocol by 11.0 and 7.6 percentage points, respectively. In an ablation study, supervising only executable commands rather than the Actor's full response raises 3B WebShop success from 52.3% to 75.0%.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 ECOS：用环境结果（命令级 advantage）校准 on-policy 自蒸馏中教师偏好的权重，并据此筛选值得强化的自写反思与技能，在 ALFWorld、WebShop 上验证效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按环境反馈决定信任哪些自生成监督、只监督可执行命令的贡献分配做法，可能可供核查 LVR 中轨迹/视觉证据监督的信度加权与信息坍缩问题，但属纯文本 agent 线索，需较多核查。
